payload.title: Match HTTP response bodies
payload.goal: Add an `expectBody` option (a substring, or a RegExp in the API) and a `--expect-body` CLI flag, so `http-get:` and `https-get:` resources count as available only once the response body contains the text.
acceptance: Against a local server, `expectBody` on an `http-get:` resource keeps waiting while the GET body does not contain the text, then succeeds once it does; a RegExp works the same way in the API.
It fails with the usual timeout error when the body never matches.
The options check rejects `expectBody` on a HEAD (`http:` or `https:`) resource straight away, with a clear message that names `expectBody` and the `-get` form to use instead.
The CLI takes `--expect-body <text>`, exits 0 once the body matches and non-zero on a timeout.
bin/usage.txt, README.md and index.d.ts document the option, the type tests cover it, and `npm test` (lint, types and mocha) passes.

Implemented `expectBody` / `--expect-body` for this task.

**Changes**
- `lib/wait-on.js`: added `expectBody` (non-empty string or RegExp) to the Joi schema; fail-fast rejection when any `http:`/`https:` HEAD resource is used with it; GET polling now requires status success plus body match (substring `includes` or RegExp `test`, with `lastIndex` reset for `/g`/`/y`), reading the raw text payload; works with `reverse` via the existing negation.
- `bin/wait-on`: added `--expect-body <text>` (string form, CLI wins over config), erroring clearly on a missing value.
- `bin/usage.txt`, `README.md`, `index.d.ts`: documented the option; `test/types.test-d.ts` covers string and RegExp forms.
- Verified: `npm run lint` and `npm run test:types` pass; `test/validation.mocha.js` passes; stubbed-axios checks confirmed wait-then-succeed, RegExp (incl. global flag), JSON-object bodies, reverse mode, and the usual `Timed out waiting for` error; CLI exits 1 on HEAD rejection and on empty `--expect-body`.
